route.description: A = the public definition changes and the molecule must be rebuilt: a slot, property or event is added, removed, renamed, or keeps its name and takes different content, a different type or a different purpose — the test is that EXISTING MARKUP HAS TO BE REWRITTEN. B = a minor change: appearance, wording, or a defect — including a defect the contract described as if it were intended, where correcting that sentence is part of the edit. C = the molecule is a shell AND the behaviour to change lives in its parent. D = the request is not about changing this molecule.

rationale.description: One or two sentences, in the user's language, saying WHY this route. It is shown to the user, and on route D it is the whole answer they get.

expectedArtifacts.description: Which artifacts the change is expected to touch. EMPTY on routes A and D — A hands the work over to a rebuild and D writes nothing. At least one on routes B and C; on C the list is CONDITIONAL — what would be touched if the fix lands in this project, since one of C's legal outcomes ('the base component is where this belongs') writes nothing at all.

definitionElements.description: Only on route A: the named slots, properties or events whose change forces EXISTING MARKUP to be rewritten — added, removed, renamed, or taking different content, a different type or a different purpose. E.g. 'slot Detail', 'property pageSize', 'event rowClick'. A corrected sentence in the contract is NOT one of these. Empty on every other route. This list is what pre-fills the rebuild clarification, so a vague entry costs the user a round trip.
